correctness.rationale: For every integer m≥2 the independent supports of C6 comprise precisely alternating triples {0,2,4},{1,3,5} or one of three opposite pairs. Thus Ind(C6[K_m]) splits as two joins of three discrete m-point fibers plus exactly 3m² cross edges; relative H1 is the augmentation kernel of oriented cross-edge module with parity-swap sign ε, while H2 is the sum of two threefold tensor products of U_i=ker(sum:Z^m→Z) with Koszul permutation signs. A long exact sequence proves free integral homology, wedge counts and equivariance. Independent chain-boundary modular rank enumerations (not the supplied checker) yielded m=2: f=(12,36,16), Betti H1=11,H2=2; m=3: (18,81,54), (26,16); m=4: (24,144,128), (47,54). Rotation character averages give b1=m(m−1)/2 and b2=((m−1)^3+2(m−1))/3; normal fiber permutations and cycle rotation kill all rational invariants for W_m. The wedge splitting is only nonequivariant, rational quotient does not determine integral quotient torsion.
